experiments.title: UNVEIL
experiments.summary: A real Sentinel-2 satellite scene hides under hexagons. Lift as few as you can, then say what it is: crater, delta, glacier, mine. A new place every day, 63 in all.
experiments.tagline: Lift the hexagons. Name the place from space.

cover.alt: Slate hexagon tiles over a satellite image, a few lifted to show green evaporation ponds
cover.label: Open UNVEIL

experiments.title: The Composing Ark, 1650
experiments.summary: Compose four-part music the way Athanasius Kircher's 1650 Arca Musarithmica did. Choose Latin words, let the ark pick a rod of numbers, choose a row, and hear the counterpoint, with every note from Kircher's own tables.
experiments.tagline: Kircher's 1650 music machine: numbers in, four voices out.

cover.alt: The ark's lifted rod: Kircher's numbers for four voices with the notes they become, under the syllables A-ve Ma-ri-a
cover.label: Open The Composing Ark

experiments.note: KIRCHER 1650 · FOUR VOICES · PLAYS IN YOUR BROWSER

experiments.title: Longitude, 1714
experiments.summary: Navigate an 18th-century ship by dead reckoning. The noon sun gives your latitude; nothing gives your longitude. Find the island before the water runs out, then sail the same voyage again with Harrison's clock. A new voyage every day.
experiments.tagline: Find the island without knowing how far west you are.

cover.alt: A Mercator sea chart of the North Atlantic: a dotted reckoned track from Cádiz and the gold track the ship really sailed, ending at Hispaniola beside Puerto Rico
cover.label: Open Longitude, 1714

experiments.note: DAILY VOYAGE · DEAD RECKONING · HARRISON'S CLOCK

experiments.title: Map Monsters
experiments.summary: Sea monsters and dragons on maps and in books, 1265–1873: the walrus drawn as an elephant, the kraken that became a giant squid, the dragons that fled to the sky. Three plates, each redrawn or cut straight from the real scans.

cover.alt: Two versions of one plate side by side: whale, walrus and sea-unicorn redrawn on the left, and cut from old maps and books on the right
